edges.description: Tick inoculation exposes monocytes and macrophages to E. chaffeensis organisms capable of intracellular replication.
Entry into the mononuclear-phagocyte lineage creates a host cell compartment in which the organism can preserve an early-endosome-like vacuole.
Vacuolar E. chaffeensis delivers Etf-2 to RAB5-GTP on the organism-containing vacuole.
Vacuolar infection delivers Etf-3, which redirects host ferritin to ferritinophagy.
Intracellular E. chaffeensis remains dependent on bacterial ribosomal translation.
Blocking RAB5-dependent vacuole maturation helps intracellular E. chaffeensis avoid progression toward a degradative compartment.
Ferritinophagy-derived labile iron supports intracellular Ehrlichia proliferation.
Persistent monocytotropic infection elicits T-cell and neutrophil inflammatory responses that can become injurious in severe disease.
Intracellular replication and inflammatory host responses produce the characteristic fever, cytopenias, and elevated hepatic transaminases.
Dysregulated TNF-rich and neutrophil-amplified inflammation contributes to the severe systemic inflammatory arm of HME.
The IOE mouse reproduces the dysregulated TNF-alpha CD8 T-cell and neutrophil-amplified immunopathology of fatal human ehrlichiosis.
edges.limitations: The infecting organism is Ehrlichia sp. HF (IOE), not E. chaffeensis, so the immunopathology is a surrogate-species model of human HME.
